newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RBNZ forecasts assume 90-day bank bills at 9 pct.
newsitem.headline: RBNZ forecasts assume 90-day bank bills at 9 pct.

text.p: The Reserve Bank of New Zealand said on Tuesday that forecasts in its six monthly monetary policy statement assumed 90-day bank bills would be at nine percent through the forecast period.
In its previous forecasts the bank assumed the bills would be at 10.0 percent over the entire period of the projections.
The 90-day bills were at 7.9 percent on Monday.
The bank noted short term interest rates had fallen quite rapidly recently as investors anticipated it would accommodate some easing in the stance of policy.

"Earlier in the period there had been a sense among professional investors that the bank would not be happy with any fall in short term interest rates. In a sense this was a fair perception. As much of the recent inflation pressure had been concentrated in the housing sector and in the non-tradeables sector more generally, the bank had been reluctant to see interest rates fall," the bank said.
"As a result the exchange rate was allowed to appreciate a little more than might otherwise have been the case."
